newsitem.title: USA: Suprema sees current qtr loss of $0.32/sh.
newsitem.headline: Suprema sees current qtr loss of $0.32/sh.

text.p: Suprema Specialties Inc said Monday it will report in the current quarter a $1.6 million loss, or about 32 cents per share, as a result of a sale-leaseback transaction involving production equipment.

The cheese manufacturer said the loss, after taking into account the net effect of corporate income tax, will result from the completed sale of its interest in production and operating equipment to Fleet Capital Corp. for about $9.5 million.

Under the agreement, Suprema said it will lease back the equipment for eight years. The sale will reduce Suprema's fixed assets by about $11.1 million, reduce its debt by $4.9 million and boost its cash by $3.7 million.

"Although this sale-leaseback transaction will negatively affect our results for the quarter and year ended June 30, 1997, it gives the company a stronger balance sheet with reduced debt and increased cash," said Suprema chief executive officer Mark Cocchiola.
Suprema officials could not be immediately reached for other details about Fleet Capital Corp.

On another matter, Suprema said its board of directors has authorized the company to spend up to $1.6 million to repurchase, from time to time depending on market conditions, about 400,000 shares of the company's stock.
The company had 5.0 million common shares as of March 31, compared with 3.3 million the same time last year.
